extracted.intended_audience: Prospective grantseekers (nonprofit organizations and government entities) seeking funding from The Heinz Endowments, especially those in southwestern Pennsylvania.
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for nonprofit and government applicants on eligibility, what program areas the Endowments funds, how to submit a Letter of Inquiry or general application via Blackbaud, the review and due-diligence process, and post-award requirements and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program areas funded
rubrics_metrics.description: The Heinz Endowments awards grants in these areas: Arts & Culture; Civic Participation; Climate, Environment & Health; Community & Economic Development; Food Systems; Veterans; and Workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should carefully review the goals of each program strategy before applying and can find a list of previously awarded grants on the Grants Awarded page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic focus (regional eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: We concentrate our efforts and resources in southwestern Pennsylvania (SWPA). Given our primarily regional focus, the foundation is generally unable to consider applications for funding outside the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, unless the proposal is expressly for the benefit of residents of the SWPA region or state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicant types
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation funds organizations classified as tax-exempt under Section 501(c)(3) of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code and as public charities under Section 509(a) of that code. Organizations and government entities that are federally tax-exempt may also apply. Individuals and for-profit organizations are not eligible for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please verify your organization’s status in GuideStar/Candid to make sure that it is properly listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of organization status (GuideStar/Candid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please verify your organization’s status in GuideStar/Candid to make sure that it is properly listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use a general application vs. an LOI
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantseekers working with Endowments’ staff should complete a general application. Grantseekers not yet working with Endowments’ staff should submit a short LOI to enter the process for funding consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both our general application and LOI are accepted on a rolling basis. Program teams will communicate directly with you about the relevant timeline for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: General application required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The general application requires a descriptive proposal narrative, information about the organization’s annual or project budget, audited financial statements, and a signed Patriot Act compliance statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the general application questions is available in PDF format (link provided on the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of Inquiry (LOI) specifics and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The short LOI takes about 10 minutes to complete. We aim to respond to all inquiries within 45 days. If approved, the organization will be invited to complete a general application that builds from the LOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission platform and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and LOIs are submitted via the Blackbaud Applicant & Grantee Portal. The site provides instructions on how to set up a Blackbaud ID and navigate the application process, and a link to access in-process applications or reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program team review and due diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Our program team will carefully review each application. If the proposal could be a good fit, program officers will perform additional due diligence, which might involve site visits, in person or virtual meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program teams will communicate directly with applicants about relevant timelines and any additional information or visits required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision timeline and influencing factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported proposals will then move through the approval and funding process, which typically takes between 60 and 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline is influenced by several factors including the request amount, timing of our Board meetings, and alignment to one of our seven priority strategies. Our team will communicate along the way to ensure you understand the approval and funding schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-approval requirements and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved, grantees will receive a notification packet including a grant agreement, guidelines for follow-up reporting and press release information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment will be made shortly after the signed grant agreement is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and contact for questions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any questions or concerns, reach out to [email protected].

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Endowments' goals and impact on the Pittsburgh region
rubrics_metrics.description: Heinz Endowments grant recipients have undergone a thoughtful and rigorous selection process that determined their work advances our efforts to help the Pittsburgh region prosper as a vibrant center of arts and culture; civic participation; and social, economic and environmental sustainability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should ensure proposals clearly demonstrate how the proposed work advances the Endowments' regional goals and the relevant program strategy.
